marks.gloss_en: that city fasts and sounds the alarm
what is pestilence? a city that sends out five hundred foot-soldiers, and three dead went out of it in three days one after the other -- this is pestilence
for these they sound the alarm in every place: for blight
an incident: Elders went down from Jerusalem to their cities and decreed a fast because there was seen in Ashkelon blight as much as fills an oven's mouth
for every trouble that may [lit. should not] come upon the community they sound the alarm

he drew a circle and stood in it and said before Him: Master of the world, Your children have turned their faces to me, for I am like a member of Your household; I swear by Your great name that I will not move from here until You have mercy on Your children
it fell properly, until Israel went out of Jerusalem to the Temple Mount because of the rain
Shimon ben Shetach sent to him: were you not Choni, I would decree ostracism upon you
the mishna (lemma): and likewise where rain ceased between one rain and the next, etc. [the elided ruling: they sound the alarm immediately]
for these they sound the alarm on Shabbat: for a city that gentiles surrounded
ורמינהי: רביעה ראשונה ושניה לשאול, שלישית להתענות! -- the baraita puts fasting at the third rainfall, the mishna at the first (kind tanya under protest: the marker is ורמינהי)
the mishna (lemma): the order of these fasts that is stated -- in the first rainfall

הכי קאמר: the stated order applies when all three rainfalls passed without rain; in the first rainfall the case is rain that fell, was sown and did not sprout or changed -- for that they sound the alarm immediately (= p_yehuda_hachi_kaamar)
Rav Yehuda: this is what it says -- the order of fasts stated, when? at a time when the first, second and third rainfall passed and rain did not fall
Rav Nachman: specifically 'changed'; but 'dried' -- no [they do not sound the alarm immediately]
if they were fasting and rain fell for them before sunrise -- they do not complete [the fast]
an incident: they decreed a fast in Lod, and rain fell for them before midday
